priceSnapshot.note: THE BREAKDOWN DID NOT FOLLOW THROUGH, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE REPORT. Yesterday's midday session recorded a confirmed 4H close below $63,000 at 62,746.1 and a 62,500.0 session low; the desk honoured its eleven-session rule and trimmed the spot core. In the twenty-one and a half hours since that snapshot at 63,085.3, price has gone precisely nowhere - it sits at 63,106.0, twenty dollars higher, having traded a 62,844.1-63,296.9 band. That is a 0.72% range against a 2.57% daily ATR: the market has compressed to roughly a quarter of a normal day's travel immediately after breaking a level it had defended for eleven sessions. A break that is not sold is a failed break, and price closing back above $63,000 and holding it through an entire overnight and Asian session is the single most informative thing on the chart. The confirmation is in the derivative tape: CoinGlass 24h liquidations have collapsed 81.19% to $67.66M and 24h volume is down 58.35% to $81.23B. Nobody is being forced anywhere. Session range measured from the midday snapshot is 62,844.1 - 63,296.9.

reduceIf.confirmation: The long-term spot core was already trimmed 20% yesterday at 63,085.3 when the $63,000 rail fired, so the first notch is spent and the core now HOLDS. The SECOND notch goes only on a 4H CLOSE below $62,279.54 - the 933.01K CoinGlass band that is the heaviest single feature anywhere on the 48h map, 1.31% under spot and never tagged (yesterday's 62,500.0 low stopped 220 points short of it). A close through that band means the largest pool of forced flow on the chart has been consumed rather than defended, and the next measured shelf behind it is 314.24K at 60,642.52, a 3.90% drop with nothing verified in between. The nearer tactical line is the 62,844.1 session low: losing it does not trim the core, it closes the futures long.

addIf.confirmation: The core gets rebuilt on a 4H CLOSE back above $63,269.18, the 4H EMA200. That average is the only long average still sitting beneath price on any timeframe and it is the exact line the market lost yesterday; spot at 63,106.0 is 163 points beneath it, so this is a near trigger, not a distant one. Note the qualifier: CLOSE, not touch - the last four completed 4H bars closed 62,997.1, 63,052.6, 63,078.8 and 63,100.9, a staircase walking up into the average without yet clearing it. A break of the 63,296.9 session high that holds into a 4H close is what turns this coil into an add.

decisionBox.changed: Five things changed versus yesterday's midday report, and the first two pull in opposite directions. ONE: the breakdown failed. Price reclaimed $63,000 and has held it for twenty-one hours in a 0.72% band, the tightest compression of the drawdown, so the bias moves from bearish back to range with a bullish tilt. TWO: the ETF tape turned genuinely hostile - Farside now publishes 31 Jul at MINUS $265.4M, the largest single-day outflow since 24 Jul, led by IBIT -122.7 and FBTC -54.6, which breaks the two-session inflow streak the last three reports leaned on. THREE: positioning FLIPPED sides. CoinGlass 24h Long/Short read 49.65%/50.35% yesterday, a balanced 0.99; it now reads 42.93%/57.07%, a skew of 0.75 - the crowd is short for the first time in this sequence, which is the mechanical argument for an upside squeeze rather than a cascade. FOUR: the liquidation map re-formed almost symmetrically around spot - 863.60K at 63,544.51 just 0.70% above against 933.01K at 62,279.54 1.31% below, so the heavier pool is below but the CLOSER pool is above. FIVE: the 1H MACD histogram crossed positive (+54.88 from -131.08), the first positive momentum reading on that timeframe since the breakdown began.

liquidation.note: THE HEAVIEST SINGLE BAND ON THE MAP AND STILL THE DAY'S UNFINISHED BUSINESS. It is the reason the second reduce notch is parked here rather than at a round number.

It is 93% as heavy as the 933.01K band beneath, but it sits at half the distance, so on a pure gravity reading the nearer pull is UP. Read together with the 42.93%/57.07% long/short skew - the crowd is short - this is the measured target for a squeeze, and it is the first take-profit on the futures long.

This is the thin patch between the market and the magnet: at one tenth the weight of the 933.01K band it offers almost no resistance, which is why the futures stop is set at 62,690, underneath this reading rather than above it. An ordinary sweep of the session low reaches this band; a real breakdown goes straight through it toward 62,279.

336.26K, 1.64% above spot and the second band up. It is 39% of the weight of the 63,544.51 shelf, so a squeeze that clears the first magnet meets materially thinner air on the way here. atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC over 64 sessions through the in-progress 2026-08-01 UTC candle, seeded on a 14-bar simple average of true range then Wilder-smoothed. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), then ATR = (ATRprev x 13 + TR) / 14. ATR has CONTRACTED from yesterday's 1,707.49 to 1,618.76 (-5.2%), because the in-progress daily candle has so far covered only 63,143.5 - 62,889.4 = $254, against the completed 2026-07-31 range of $2,888. At 2.57% of spot a normal day covers about $1,619; today has used 16% of that in fifteen hours. That compression is the setup, and it is also why the futures stop can sit only 416 points away without being noise: 416 is a quarter of an ATR but 1.6x the entire realised range of the current daily candle.

etfFlows.note: THE INFLOW STREAK IS BROKEN AND THIS IS THE CLEAREST BEARISH INPUT IN THE REPORT. Farside's daily Bitcoin ETF table has now published 31 Jul at MINUS $265.4M NET OUTFLOW, the largest single-day outflow since 24 Jul (-240.1), led by IBIT -122.7, FBTC -54.6, BITB -17.8 and ARKB -17.5, with a further -52.6 across the smaller funds and not a single fund printing a meaningful inflow. That follows 30 Jul at +233.1 and 29 Jul at +32.1, so the two-session inflow streak the last three reports leaned on is over and streakDays resets to 0. The uncomfortable read is that institutions sold $265M into a session where price barely moved: the selling was absorbed. That is a different market from the one on 29-30 July, where $265M of buying could not stop a 2.75% decline. Absorption in both directions is what a coil is.

calibration.rollingRecord: Yesterday's midday report called bearish with a 45% bear weight and trimmed the spot core 20% at 63,085.3. Twenty-one hours later spot is 63,106.0 - twenty dollars HIGHER - so the trim neither helped nor hurt materially, and by the strict test of 'did acting beat not acting' it did not. The direction call was wrong over the following session: the report weighted bearish at 45% against range at 33%, and the market delivered the tightest range of the drawdown. The second reduce level at 62,205 did not fire (session low 62,844.1, 639 points clear) and the 63,283 add level did not fire either (session high 63,296.9 touched it on a wick but no 4H closed above it). This is the second consecutive session where the desk's directional lean has been overtaken by compression rather than movement.
calibration.note: The honest lesson from the last two sessions is about magnitude, not direction. The midday report was right that $63,000 was a real structural line and right that the map had re-formed lower - it was wrong to convert that into a 45% bear weight, because the same map showed the magnet UNTAGGED 295 points below the low, which is a setup for a coil rather than a cascade. Today's report deliberately holds the range weight highest at 42% and expresses the bullish tilt through a small, tightly-stopped futures long rather than through a directional bet on the core.
